articles.title: POLITICAL ROW: Vande Mataram Controversy Intensifies After Congress Sings Only Two Verses
articles.description: The political controversy over Vande Mataram continues to intensify, with the latest dispute emerging from the Congress convention in Goa. After the song was reportedly sung only partially in Goa, questions are being raised over Congress’s position on the national song. The controversy follows the incident at the Congress headquarters on Independence Day, where questions were also raised over the singing of Vande Mataram. The political debate has now expanded after Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur reportedly refused to sing Vande Mataram, citing constitutional rights. Meanwhile, Congress leader Nana Patole has claimed that the party high command had conveyed a message to sing only two verses, adding another dimension to the controversy. The BJP has launched a sharp attack on Congress over the issue. BJP MP Kangana Ranaut compared Congress’s approach to Vande Mataram with Pakistan and alleged that the party has moved from being anti-BJP to being “anti-national.” She described Vande Mataram as a symbol of India’s collective consciousness and questioned why there was opposition to singing the complete song. Union Minister Giriraj Singh also targeted the Congress leadership, alleging that the party has changed from its earlier form and accusing its leadership of insulting Vande Mataram. He also criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, alleging that he follows the direction of the Gandhi family.

articles.title: Govt presses Meta on WhatsApp username row
articles.description: New Delhi: The government's hard talk with Meta has led to action and increased sensitivity on the issue of child sexual abuse material (CSAM), IT Ministry sources said on Tuesday, adding that the Centre has been unequivocal that such content is a clear violation and there is no safe harbour when law is violated in this manner.Sources said the government's intent is not about censorship or restricting coverage in any way, but ensuring Indian laws and norms are followed and that social media harms are mitigated. "The message has gone home," they said.Also read: Meta, YouTube, TikTok face thousands of lawsuits in the US over kids’ mental health: What we knowDuring discussions, Meta explained how its algorithms and systems work, ministry sources said, noting that discussions are on and such matters involve "judgment calls, and tweaks".On the WhatsApp username row, sources said the matter is under examination as it doesn't involve just that particular platform, but other messaging apps as well.Sources said concerns over social media harms is not something specific only to India, it is a concern shared by other nations including Australia, the UK and France.Platforms have a responsibility to address social media harms and strike the right balance, sources asserted.On AI labelling, the ministry official said the law is clear that synthetically generated content must be labelled, and that responsibility lies at three levels, including with platforms. Platforms must comply accordingly, they added. PTI

articles.title: Nitin Nabin’s New BJP Team: Experience, Youth & Women Power Take Centre Stage
articles.description: BJP president Nitin Nabin has unveiled his first national team, bringing together seasoned organisational leaders, younger faces and prominent comebacks. The new line-up includes 13 national vice presidents, eight general secretaries and 16 national secretaries, with BL Santhosh continuing as the party’s organisational powerhouse. Ram Madhav and Smriti Irani return to key national roles, while several familiar faces have been dropped. Uttar Pradesh gets strong representation ahead of next year’s Assembly elections, while the team also reflects regional and social diversity. Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the new team, calling it a blend of experience and energy. For Nitin Nabin, the message is clear: consolidation, continuity and organisational strength.

articles.title: BIG CONTROVERSY: Naxalism Victims Question Leaders Calling Themselves ‘Ideological Naxals’
articles.description: A political controversy has erupted across the country over the phrase “ideological Naxal” after Prime Minister Narendra Modi referred to the term during his Independence Day address from the Red Fort. The debate intensified after senior Congress leader P Chidambaram described himself as an “ideological Naxal” in a social media post, saying he was proud of it. Other opposition leaders have also commented on the issue, keeping the political debate alive. Amid the political exchange, victims and families affected by Naxal violence have now come forward to express their pain and anger. Through banners, posters and public statements, they have questioned the use of the term and asked political leaders to consider the experiences of people who have actually suffered from Maoist violence. One victim from Chhattisgarh’s Bastar region recalled that his father, a security personnel, was killed in an IED blast allegedly carried out by Naxals in Dantewada in 2018. He said his family had to carry his father’s funeral bier and questioned whether political leaders who claim to support “ideological Naxals” also stand with families of personnel killed in Naxal attacks. Another victim from the Kanker region described being forced to leave his village and later suffering severe injuries in an alleged IED blast. He said he lost one leg and sustained serious injuries to the other, leaving him struggling to rebuild his life. The victims have appealed to political leaders to understand the long-term impact of Naxal violence on families, villages and security personnel. They also expressed concern over statements that, according to them, could encourage the return of Naxal ideology in areas that have experienced years of violence.

articles.title: In 1862, Abraham Lincoln signed a law that gave Americans a chance to claim 160 acres of free land. What happened next transformed the American West forever
articles.description: In 1862, President Abraham Lincoln enacted the Homestead Act, granting land to settlers eager to populate the West. This initiative allowed qualified individuals to claim 160 acres after five years of cultivation, significantly altering America's landscape. However, it also resulted in the displacement of Indigenous populations. The act prevailed for over a hundred years, leaving a lasting impact on the country's growth and development.
